summary: Even people who may not do the avodah are allowed to shecht a korban, so their wrong thoughts can also make it pasul. If they caught the blood with a wrong thought, a kosher Kohen should catch more blood if there is still some.

chunks.en: All those not fit for the avodah who shechted,
chunks.st: With regard to all those who are unfit for Temple service who slaughtered an offering,

words.en: the ones who are not fit
words.note: Not fit to do the avodah in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: their shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: their slaughter is valid,

chunks.en: Because shechitah is kosher when done by non-Kohanim,
chunks.st: as the slaughter of an offering is valid ab initio when performed even by non-priests,

chunks.en: by women, and by servants,
chunks.st: by women, by Canaanite slaves,

chunks.en: and by people who are tamei, even for the holiest korbanos,
chunks.st: and by ritually impure individuals. And this is the halakha even with regard to offerings of the most sacred order,

chunks.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ טְמֵאִים נוֹגְעִים בַּבָּשָׂר.
chunks.en: as long as the tamei people do not touch the meat.
chunks.st: provided that the ritually impure will not touch the flesh of the slaughtered animal, thereby rendering it impure.

chunks.en: So they can make it pasul with their thoughts.
chunks.st: Therefore, these unfit individuals can disqualify the offering with prohibited intent,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if one of them intended to partake of the offering beyond its designated time or outside its designated area.

chunks.en: And all of them, if they caught the blood
chunks.st: And with regard to all of them, in a case where they collected the blood

chunks.en: planning for after its time or outside its place,
chunks.st: with the intent to offer it beyond its designated time or outside its designated area,

chunks.en: if there is still life-blood left,
chunks.st: if there is blood of the soul that remains in the animal,

words.note: The blood that pours out at shechitah, which the korban needs.

chunks.en: a kosher Kohen should catch blood again.
chunks.st: the priest fit for Temple service should again collect the blood and sprinkle it on the altar.

summary: Mistakes with the blood can sometimes be fixed: give it back to a kosher Kohen, to the right hand, or to a holy vessel. If it was put in the wrong place on the mizbeach, a kosher Kohen can catch new blood if there is still some.

chunks.en: If a kosher Kohen caught the blood and gave it to one who is not fit,
chunks.st: If the priest fit for Temple service collected the blood in a vessel and gave the vessel to an unfit person,

chunks.en: it should be given back to the kosher one.
chunks.st: that person should return it to the fit priest.

chunks.en: If he caught it in his right hand and moved it to his left,
chunks.st: If the priest collected the blood in a vessel in his right hand and moved it to his left hand,

chunks.en: he should move it back to his right.
chunks.st: he should return it to his right hand.

chunks.he: קִבֵּל בִּכְלִי קֹדֶשׁ וְנָתַן בִּכְלִי חֹל,
chunks.en: If he caught it in a holy vessel and put it in a regular vessel,
chunks.st: If the priest collected the blood in a sacred vessel and placed it in a non-sacred vessel,

words.note: A regular vessel, not made holy for the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: he should put it back in a holy vessel.
chunks.st: he should return the blood to a sacred vessel.

chunks.he: נִשְׁפַּךְ מִן הַכְּלִי עַל הָרִצְפָּה וַאֲסָפוֹ,
chunks.en: If it spilled from the vessel onto the floor and he gathered it,
chunks.st: If the blood spilled from the vessel onto the floor and he gathered it from the floor,

chunks.en: it is kosher. If one put it on the ramp,
chunks.st: it is valid. If an unfit person placed the blood upon the ramp

chunks.en: on a part that is not over the base,
chunks.st: or on the wall of the altar that is not opposite the base of the altar,

chunks.en: or he put blood that goes below
chunks.st: or if he placed the blood that is to be placed below

chunks.en: above, or blood that goes above,
chunks.st: the red line above the red line, or if he placed the blood that is to be placed above

chunks.en: below; or blood that goes inside,
chunks.st: the red line below the red line, or if he placed the blood that is to be placed inside

chunks.en: outside; or blood that goes outside,
chunks.st: the Sanctuary outside the Sanctuary or the blood that is to be placed outside

chunks.en: inside, then if there is still life-blood left,
chunks.st: the Sanctuary inside the Sanctuary, then if there is blood of the soul that remains in the animal,

chunks.en: a kosher Kohen should catch blood again.
chunks.st: the priest fit for Temple service should again collect the blood and sprinkle it on the altar.

summary: If he shechted planning to eat a part that is not usually eaten, or burn a part that is not usually burned, the korban is still kosher. A thought about less than an olive-size also does not ruin it.

chunks.en: One who shechts the korban planning to eat
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters an offering with the intent to eat, beyond its designated time or outside its designated area,

chunks.en: something that is not usually eaten,
chunks.st: an item whose typical manner is such that one does not partake
chunks.stMore: of it, e.g., the portions of the offering consumed on the altar,

chunks.en: or to burn something that is not usually burned,
chunks.st: or with the intent to burn, beyond its designated time or outside its designated area, an item whose typical manner is such that one does not burn it on the altar, e.g., the meat of the offering,

chunks.en: it is kosher. Rabbi Eliezer says it is pasul.
chunks.st: the offering is fit, and Rabbi Eliezer deems it unfit.

chunks.en: If he planned to eat something that is usually eaten,
chunks.st: One who slaughters an offering with the intent to eat, beyond its designated time or outside its designated area, an item whose typical manner is such that one does partake of it,

chunks.en: or to burn something that is usually burned,
chunks.st: or with the intent to burn, beyond its designated time or outside its designated area, an item whose typical manner is such that one does burn it on the altar,

chunks.en: but less than an olive-size,
chunks.st: but his intent was to partake or burn less than an olive-bulk,

chunks.he: כָּשֵׁר. לֶאֱכֹל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וּלְהַקְטִיר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת,
chunks.en: it is kosher. To eat half an olive-size and burn half an olive-size,
chunks.st: the offering is fit. If his intent was to eat half an olive-bulk and to burn half an olive-bulk beyond its designated time or outside its designated area,

chunks.en: it is kosher, because eating and burning do not add up together.
chunks.st: the offering is fit, because eating and burning do not join together.

summary: Planning to eat parts like the skin, bones or horns after their time or outside their place does not ruin the korban. These parts are not counted as meat for the rules of piggul, nosar or tumah.

chunks.en: One who shechts the korban planning to eat
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters an offering with the intent to eat, beyond its designated time or outside its designated area,

chunks.en: an olive-size of the skin,
chunks.st: an olive-bulk from the hide,

chunks.en: of the gravy,
chunks.st: or from the gravy,

chunks.en: of the spices left at the bottom of the pot,
chunks.st: or from the spices
chunks.stMore: that amass at the bottom of the pot together with small amounts of meat,

words.note: Spices and bits of meat stuck at the bottom of the pot.

chunks.en: of a neck tendon,
chunks.st: or from a tendon in the neck,

chunks.en: of the bones,
chunks.st: or from the bones,

chunks.en: of the sinews,
chunks.st: or from the tendons,

chunks.en: of the hooves, or of the horns,
chunks.st: or from the horns, or from the hooves,

chunks.he: חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ אוֹ חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ, כָּשֵׁר,
chunks.en: after its time or outside its place, it is kosher,
chunks.st: the offering is fit

chunks.en: and one is not punished for them because of
chunks.st: and one is not liable to receive karet for it, neither due to

chunks.en: piggul, nosar, or tumah.
chunks.st: the prohibition of piggul, if the sacrificial rites were performed with the intent to partake of the offering beyond its designated time, nor due to the prohibition of leftover meat beyond the designated time, nor due to the prohibition against partaking of the meat while ritually impure.

words.note: Meat of a korban left over after the time to eat it.

summary: Planning to eat an unborn calf, a hen's eggs, or other things that are not really part of the korban does not make it piggul. One who eats them is not punished with kares for piggul, nosar or tumah.

chunks.en: One who shechts holy animals planning to eat
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters sacrificial female animals with the intent to eat

chunks.en: an unborn calf or the afterbirth outside,
chunks.st: the fetus of those animals or their placenta outside the designated area,

words.note: What comes out after a calf is born.

chunks.en: did not make it piggul.
chunks.st: he has not rendered the offering piggul. Likewise,

chunks.he: הַמּוֹלֵק תּוֹרִין בִּפְנִים לֶאֱכֹל בֵּיצֵיהֶם בַּחוּץ,
chunks.en: One who does melikah on doves inside, planning to eat their eggs outside,
chunks.st: in the case of one who pinches doves, i.e., slaughters them for sacrifice by cutting the napes of their necks with his fingernail, with the intent to eat their eggs that are still in their bodies outside the designated area,

words.note: The way a Kohen shechts a bird korban, with his fingernail.

chunks.en: did not make it piggul.
chunks.st: he has not rendered the offering piggul.
chunks.stMore: This is because the fetus, the placenta, and the eggs are not considered part of the body of the animal or the bird. For the same reason,

chunks.en: The milk of holy animals and the eggs of doves,
chunks.st: one who consumes the milk of sacrificial female animals or the eggs of doves

chunks.en: one is not punished for them because of
chunks.st: is not liable to receive karet for it, neither due to

chunks.en: piggul, nosar, or tumah.
chunks.st: the prohibition of piggul, nor due to the prohibition of notar, nor due to the prohibition against partaking of the meat while ritually impure.

summary: Some wrong thoughts do not ruin a korban: leaving its blood for tomorrow, putting blood in the wrong place, having tamei people eat it, or breaking the Pesach's bones. Only thoughts about the wrong time or place, or the wrong purpose for a Pesach or chatas, make it pasul.

chunks.en: If he shechted it planning to leave its blood
chunks.st: If one slaughters the animal in order to leave its blood

chunks.en: or its parts for the mizbeach until tomorrow,
chunks.st: or its sacrificial portions for the next day,

chunks.en: or to take them outside,
chunks.st: or to remove them outside
chunks.stMore: the designated area, but not in order to sacrifice them the next day,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says it is pasul,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda deems the offering unfit,

chunks.en: and the Sages say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem it fit.

chunks.en: If he shechted it planning to put the blood on
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters the animal in order to place

chunks.en: the ramp, on a part not over the base,
chunks.st: the blood upon the ramp or on the wall of the altar that is not opposite the base of the altar,

chunks.en: or to put blood that goes below
chunks.st: or in order to place the blood that is to be placed above

chunks.en: above, or blood that goes above,
chunks.st: the red line below the red line, or to place the blood that is to be placed below

chunks.en: below; or blood that goes inside,
chunks.st: the red line above the red line, or the blood that is to be placed inside

chunks.en: outside; or blood that goes outside,
chunks.st: the Sanctuary outside the Sanctuary, or the blood that is to be placed outside

chunks.en: inside; or that tamei people will eat it,
chunks.st: the Sanctuary inside the Sanctuary; and likewise, if he slaughtered the animal with the intent that ritually impure people will partake of it,

chunks.en: or that tamei people will offer it,
chunks.st: or that ritually impure people will sacrifice it,

chunks.en: or that men without a bris will eat it,
chunks.st: or that uncircumcised people will partake of it,

chunks.en: or that men without a bris will offer it,
chunks.st: or that uncircumcised people will sacrifice it; and likewise, with regard to the Paschal offering,

chunks.he: לְשַׁבֵּר עַצְמוֹת הַפֶּסַח וְלֶאֱכֹל הֵימֶנּוּ נָא,
chunks.en: or to break the bones of the Pesach, or to eat it half-roasted,
chunks.st: if he had intent during the slaughter to break the bones of the Paschal offering, or to eat from the meat of the Paschal offering partially roasted,

chunks.en: or to mix its blood with the blood of pasul korbanos,
chunks.st: or to mix the blood of an offering with the blood of unfit
chunks.stMore: offerings, in all these cases, although he intended to perform one of these prohibited acts, some of which would render the offering unfit,

chunks.en: it is kosher. Because a thought only makes it pasul
chunks.st: the offering is fit. The reason is that intent does not render the offering unfit except in

chunks.en: if it is about after its time or outside its place,
chunks.st: cases of intent to eat or to burn the offering beyond its designated time and outside its designated area,

chunks.en: or a Pesach or chatas for the wrong purpose.
chunks.st: and in addition, the Paschal offering and the sin offering are disqualified by intent to sacrifice them not for their sake.
